newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepal impasse ends, Chand named new prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Nepal impasse ends, Chand named new prime minister.

text.p: Nepal's political crisis ended on Monday when King Birendra named Lokendra Bahadur Chand as the Himalayan kingdom's fifth prime minister in seven years.

"His Majesty the King, in accordance with...the constitution of the kingdom of Nepal, has appointed House of Representatives member Lokendra Bahadur Chand prime minister," a royal communique, broadcast by state-owned Nepal Television, said.

Palace officials said Chand, leader of the centrist Rashtriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), was expected to be formally sworn in on Tuesday by the king, who abandoned his absolute powers in 1990 but remains a constitutional monarch,
The 57-year-old Chand heads a coalition comprising the RPP, the communist Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) party and the Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP).
Chand told reporters: "I will be sworn in tomorrow when a new cabinet will also be announced."

Earlier on Monday UML General Secretary Madhav Kumar Nepal and Chand registered a joint claim to govern at the gates of King Birendra's palace. The king had set a deadline of 6.00 p.m. (1215 GMT) for claims to a new government to be staked.

The four-day crisis gripping the world's only Hindu kingdom ended swiftly hours after Sher Bahadur Deuba, who resigned last Thursday as prime minister, declared he would sit in the opposition after failing to cobble together a new coalition.

A UML leader told Reuters earlier on Monday that his party and its allies controlled 103 of 205 seats in the lower house of parliament -- just enough to survive -- and would support Chand as the new prime minister.
Chand was twice prime minister under the Panchayat system of government which lasted from 1961 until 1990 and permitted the king to rule directly over a partyless assembly.

UML officials earlier said details of the programme of the new government were being worked out. The cabinet would initially be small and would be expanded after the mandatory confidence vote Chand has to win within a month of taking office.
Nepal, which maintained self-imposed isolation until the middle of the century, is one of the world's 10 poorest nations with an annual average income of $200 a head.
Deuba's three-party coalition took over in September 1995 from the communist UML, which ruled at the head of a minority government following inconclusive polls in 1994.
Squabbling among the three ruling parties undercut Deuba's coalition and led to the defection last week of at least 10 of the RPP's 19 lawmakers to the communist side.
The next general election is not scheduled until November 1999.
